$comment: First-load budgets for the web app. Enforced by src/size-budget.test.ts; reported on
every PR by tools/report-size-budget.mjs. JSON carries no comments, so the reasoning
lives in `why` fields and in apps/web/src/size-budget.test.ts's header.
WHAT IS BUDGETED is the TOTAL first-load payload -- the page shell plus every engine
artifact a user downloads before their first operation can run -- not only per-file
sizes. Three files each growing 4% is a 4% regression that no 10%-per-file budget
notices. So `total` is the binding gate and the per-artifact lines say WHERE it went.
ORIGIN. docs/spikes/0001-wasm-engines.md measured the option-1 payload at 6,502,775
raw / 2,200,580 brotli, 82% of it PDFium, and ROADMAP item 11 records that as 'the
starting point, not a target'. The shipped build has since drifted above it: qpdf is
now built from source against our own vendored zlib and libjpeg-turbo (1,199,200 raw
against the spike's 917,305), the Rust module has grown from 15,266 to 43,072, and
the three glue files the spike listed separately now live inside one worker bundle.
The numbers below are a fresh measurement of what actually ships, not the spike's
table. pdfium.wasm's brotli size is unchanged from the spike to the byte.
TO CHANGE A BUDGET: re-measure, update `measured_brotli` AND `budget_brotli`, and say
why in the commit. An engine pin bump is the expected reason. Raising a budget to make
CI pass without knowing what grew is the thing this file exists to prevent.
WHEN THE TOTAL IS RE-RAISED TO 3%, because this file now contains two decisions that look
opposite. M1 PR B3 refused a raise at 2.6% headroom -- "raising a budget that is not
binding would spend margin nobody needed" -- and the consolidation batch took one at 2.0%.
The discriminator is not the number: it is whether the PAYLOAD grew or the MEASUREMENT
changed. Growth eats the recorded headroom and is supposed to; that is what the margin is
for, and raising it back would be refunding the thing being measured. A measurement that
stops being blind is different -- the payload was always that size, the file was simply
wrong about it -- and leaving the total there would mean this file claiming 3% while
enforcing 2.0%, which is the quiet disagreement it exists to prevent.
The residual cost is stated rather than glossed: the raise hands out 67 KB of room at the
moment the measurement got sharper, which is the moment a gate is most useful tight. What
makes that acceptable is that nothing is unwatched -- every artifact line keeps its own headroom
headroom, and the newly-visible bytes landed on `page-js`, which has one.
RAISED ONCE SO FAR, in M1 PR B2, for merge's write path. Per-artifact budgets are
recomputed only for lines that MOVED -- raising one that did not would be a silent
widening nobody asked for -- and `page` was on an absolute budget rather than a

percentage until spike 0004, when its slack alone came to more than half the
    total's -- see `headroom.why`.
HOW A RECORDING IS HELD TO THE BUILD IT DESCRIBES.
Each artifact records `measured_sha256` beside its sizes, and src/size-budget-drift.ts
turns that into a contradiction the tests can see: same bytes must mean the same
recorded numbers. Identical bytes with a different `measured_brotli` is a FALSE RECORD,
not drift, and there is no tolerance for it.
This exists because the obvious gates do not cover it. Live sizes are checked against
`budget_brotli`, and the recorded lines are checked against each other -- so a recording
that drifts CONSISTENTLY satisfies both. Measured: `engines/burrow-worker.js` was
recorded at 255,535 raw / 45,052 brotli and measured 256,255 / 45,288 on an UNCHANGED
checkout, 236 brotli bytes from a differently-built, gitignored
`bindings/burrow-wasm/pkg/`. Nothing failed. M1 PR A corrected the number; a corrected
number is not a control, because the next drift is silent in exactly the same way.
`not_byte_reproducible` is the one window this cannot close exactly, and it is declared
rather than implied: those artifacts legitimately differ per machine, so they get a
`drift_tolerance` bound instead of an equality. Every entry needs a reason. An artifact
whose bytes change WITHOUT being on that list fails -- an engine moving underneath us
should not be waved through as 'probably the toolchain'. Two of the three entries were
predicted; `engines/qpdf.wasm` was NOT, and got there by failing CI and naming itself,
which is the check working rather than the check being wrong.
THE PAGE WAS NOT ON THAT LIST, DELIBERATELY, AND IT TOOK TWO GOES -- AND IN M1 PR B3 IT
WENT ON ANYWAY. The argument below is still the right argument and it lost to a fact: the
island's minified bytes differ between architectures. The `not_byte_reproducible` entry for
`page` records what was measured, what was tried first, and what it costs. Read them
together; the paragraph below is kept rather than rewritten because the reasoning did not
stop being sound.
engine by its content-hashed URL (ADR 0014), so any engine rebuild changes index.html --
CI reported `qpdf.wasm` and `page` together for that one cause. Exempting `page` would
have meant not checking the line the design system lives on because of something
belonging to a different line.
So each artifact records TWO digests: the raw bytes, and the bytes with generated engine
hashes replaced by a fixed token. Three cases, distinguished rather than collapsed:
raw match              -> exact size equality. Nothing changed, so no tolerance.
normalised match only  -> only the quoted engine hashes differ. The artifact's own
content is unchanged, but its SIZE may wobble, because two
16-hex tokens do not compress identically. A tight absolute
bound (64 bytes), not a percentage: 2% of the page is 433
bytes and a real CSS regression could hide under that.
normalised differs     -> a real change. Must be on not_byte_reproducible or it fails.
The middle case exists because collapsing it into the first was a bug, and CI caught it:
the check reported `page: the bytes are IDENTICAL to the recording, but measured_brotli
says 21652 and the build is 21650`. The bytes were not identical. The message was the
part that was false, and a check that misdescribes what it found is worse than one that
finds nothing.
Shortening that list is the real fix and it means making `pkg/` reproducible, which is a
build change nobody has made yet.

why: Per-artifact headroom is loose (25%) because those lines are diagnostic: they say
which file moved. Total headroom is tight (10%, about 46 KB) because that line is the
gate. Both numbers were re-derived when PDFium left the payload; the paragraphs below
record what each was, what it is, and why it moved.
THE ASYMMETRY USED TO CARRY A CLAIM THAT IS NOW MEASURED FALSE. It said the total
'binds first in every case that matters -- 10% of pdfium alone is 8.5% of the total, so
a single artifact cannot reach its own ceiling without the total having failed long
before'. That holds for a LARGE artifact and not for a small one. M1's split bridge grew
`burrow_wasm_bg.wasm` by 65.7%, which blew its own ceiling while moving the total by
1.24% -- because 10% of a 36 KiB artifact is 0.15% of a 2.3 MiB payload.
So a per-artifact line CAN fire alone, and when it does it is doing the job the block
describes: saying which file moved. What it is not is a second gate, and raising one
must not be read as spending total margin -- the total is recorded separately and was
`page` is the exception and is recorded as such rather than left to look like 10%:
its budget is an ABSOLUTE 50 KiB, 58x its measurement. The reason is on that line.

THE TOTAL'S HEADROOM IS 10%, RAISED FROM 3% WHEN THE PAYLOAD FELL BY 80.7%. Not because the margin was wrong before, but because a percentage of 2.4 MB and a percentage of 462 KB are different instruments. 3% of the new total is 13,877 bytes --- inside the noise of a routine dependency bump --- so a 3% gate would fire on churn and be raised by whoever was holding it, which is how a budget becomes a formality. 10% is 46,256 bytes: large enough that an ordinary bump does not reach it, small enough that a real regression does.

AND `page` IS NO LONGER AN EXCEPTION -- IT IS ON THE PER-ARTIFACT RULE, 25%, like every other line, and `headroom.page` records that rate rather than a different one. (It was recorded as 0.10 in the first draft of this change while the line itself was derived at 1.25x, so the file disagreed with itself about a number nothing reads -- `size-budget.test.ts` consumes only `total` and `per_artifact`. An unenforced claim is the one that rots.) Its absolute 50 KiB was set when the line measured 881 bytes and was 58x it; the self-hosted typeface then took it to 22,550, and the absolute quietly became 2.3x. At the old total that was affordable. At the new one its slack alone (28,650 bytes) is more than half the entire total's headroom, so the line could absorb a regression the total was supposed to catch and report nothing. It is on the same per-artifact rule as everything else now, which is what the rest of this block already claimed the file did.

PER-ARTIFACT HEADROOM WIDENED 10% -> 25%, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE WHOLE MECHANISM. The total only catches what the lines miss if it is the TIGHTER of the two: the `catches a regression split across three files` test looks for a uniform growth that every per-artifact line passes and the total still refuses, and no such growth exists when both numbers are equal. Setting the total to 10% therefore forced the lines wider, not narrower. They lose nothing by it --- they are diagnostic, they say WHICH file moved, and the total fires first for almost any real growth anyway: 25% of qpdf.wasm alone is 18% of the payload, well past the total's 10%.

engines/qpdf.wasm.why: Built from source at the pinned version against our vendored zlib and libjpeg-turbo, so it moves with a pin bump or a build-flag change. M1 PR B2 MOVED IT BY +53,456 BROTLI (265,985 -> 319,441), and that is the single largest deliberate increase this payload has taken. The cause is qpdf's QPDFWriter and its dependencies, pulled in by adding seven entry points to EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS so merge can produce bytes on the web. ADR 0017 chose qpdf over PDFium for fidelity -- PDFium loses outlines, attachments and the /AcroForm, and the last of those silently leaves a form field that is no longer a field. PDFium already exports everything a merge needs, so choosing it would have cost ZERO bytes. This line is the price of that decision, and it is recorded here so the trade stays visible rather than becoming a number nobody can explain. M1's rotate bridge moved it +3,287 brotli (319,441 -> 322,728) by adding six `qpdf_oh_*` functions to EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS -- small beside merge's +53,456, because those seven entry points pulled in QPDFWriter and these six pull in accessors qpdf already links. It is now 70.8% of the whole payload (327,629 of 462,562), where it was 13.7%. Nothing about the artifact changed; everything about its share did. #130's WRITE VERB took it 327,493 -> 327,688, +195 brotli (+0.060%), for `qpdf_oh_replace_stream_data` and `qpdf_oh_new_null`. An A/B on one machine in one session -- the same em++ link over the same prebuilt libqpdf.a, differing only in those two entries -- whose CONTROL came out byte-identical to the shipped artifact. That control is what makes the number attributable on a line this file lists as not byte-reproducible. `engines/qpdf-not-exported.toml` has it beside merge's +53,456 and split's +3,340. #191's WEB REDACTION took it 327,688 -> 328,330, +642 brotli, for one export, `qpdf_oh_set_array_item` -- font surgery's in-place array write. Measured twice and the two agree to the byte: an A/B of the em++ link whose control is byte-identical to the shipped artifact (sha256 73f051bb...), and this build. It is 3.3x #130's +195 for one function against two, because `setArrayItem`'s code was not already linked; `engines/qpdf-not-exported.toml` has it beside the other three points.

engines/burrow-worker.js.why: The one bundle: prelude, bridge, the qpdf Emscripten glue, wasm-bindgen glue, worker main. It carried BOTH glue files until spike 0004 took PDFium out of the payload. This is the line our own worker code moves, so it is the one worth watching on an ordinary PR. M1 PR B2 added +2,628 -- the write path's nine bridge functions and the wasm-bindgen glue for the merge entry point. M1 PR B3 took it DOWN by 13 (48,092 -> 48,079): unwrapping `InputFailed` for the reply's limit detail added code, and one `innermost` helper replacing three ad-hoc unwraps took back slightly more than it cost. M1's consolidation batch added +1,125 for the pre-flight budget call and the Reply it drains. And +635 for the start-up progress message the stall bound reads (ADR 0018). M1's rotate bridge moved it +1,924 brotli: six `__burrow_qpdf_oh_*` forwarders, the `rotate` and `page_rotations` dispatch arms, and the `rotations` line in `drainReply`. ADR 0022 added +14: the `OutputRejected` kind crossing the reply boundary. RAISED IN M1's SPLIT BRIDGE, from 57,483 to 62,630, and NOT because it is close to failing: 56,936 against 57,483 is 1% of headroom where this file records 10%, and the across-the-board regression test said so first -- at +4% the worker alone would have exceeded its own budget, which would have made that test prove nothing rather than prove the total binds. The +3,591 is the multi-output protocol (ADR 0023): the part and progress messages, the cut validation, and the refusal helper the split arm shares with the others. A per-artifact budget that has drifted to 1% has stopped being diagnostic and started being a second gate, which is the thing the headroom block says it is not. SPIKE 0004 HALVED IT: 56,936 -> 33,830 brotli (both endpoints are the values recorded in this file; an earlier draft of this sentence quoted a pair that matched neither), because PDFium's 164 KB of Emscripten glue was concatenated into this bundle. The budget is recomputed from the new measurement rather than left at a number set for a bundle twice this size --- a 10% headroom over a figure that no longer describes the file is not headroom, it is a gate that cannot fire. #130's WRITE BRIDGE took it +732: the `__burrow_qpdf_oh_replace_stream_data` forwarder, `__burrow_qpdf_oh_new_null`, and the JSDoc left after the five-hazard analysis moved to `QpdfBridge::oh_replace_stream_data`. THE ANALYSIS COST 1,056 BROTLI WHEN IT LIVED HERE -- this bundle is concatenated rather than minified, so a comment is a download -- and moving it recovered 460. Right for the payload and the wrong incentive for the code, since `src/worker/` is where every pointer value in this project lives; #144 is to strip comments at build time. #191's WEB REDACTION took it +103: the `__burrow_qpdf_oh_set_array_item` forwarder and its two-line comment. The bundle is concatenated, so the comment is part of the +103.

engines/burrow_wasm_bg.wasm.why: The Rust binding: every entry point, the reply shape, and now the PRUNING POLICY and the PDF tokeniser, which split's bridge makes reachable from the web for the first time. RAISED IN M1's SPLIT BRIDGE, from 37,276 to 61,775, and the growth is the feature rather than a regression: 33,887 -> 56,159 brotli, +65.7%, of which the policy (crate::prune) and the lexer (crate::pdfsyntax) are the bulk -- roughly 1,300 lines of Rust that did not previously link into this module because no web operation reached them. The session type and the split entry point are the rest. It is a DIAGNOSTIC line, not the gate: the total is what binds, and it did not move past its budget. But this artifact is the first to blow its own ceiling while the total held, which falsifies a claim the headroom block used to make -- see there. #128's PDFSYNTAX REWRITER took it 56,777 -> 59,171 brotli, +2,394 (+4.2%), and the attribution is narrower than the change: the new modules cost NOTHING here. `ops.rs`, `contents.rs` and `strings.rs` are stripped whole by LTO -- none of their error strings are in the built wasm, checked rather than assumed -- because nothing on the web calls them until #131 does. Every one of the 2,394 bytes is the INLINE-IMAGE EXTENT derivation in `lexer.rs`, which `names_in_content` reaches and which `split` therefore runs on the web. That is the fix for a leak: the old code ended an inline image at the first `EI` standing alone, and PDFium draws text that hid behind it (ADR 0029's 2026-09-21 amendment). NOT RAISED -- 71,090 leaves 11,919 bytes, and the line is diagnostic anyway; what it diagnoses here is that a correctness fix in a shared tokeniser is payload on every route that loads the module, and that #128's other 2,000 lines are not. THE WEB HANDLE TYPE (#145) took it 59,148 -> 59,883, +735 brotli (+1.2%), and a REFACTOR that grows the module is worth a sentence rather than a shrug: `WebHandle`'s accessors are each a small monomorphised wrapper over a trait-object call that used to be written inline at the call site, so the calls did not move but their wrappers are new code. What it bought is that a handle and the session that issued it are one value -- and, for 735 bytes, that a handle outliving its session stopped compiling. #191's WEB REDACTION took it +178 brotli (+1,902 raw in the release cargo build, before wasm-bindgen): the new bridge import and its glue, because `JsQpdf` implements the whole `QpdfBridge` trait in the base module. NONE OF REDACTION ITSELF: `check-redaction-not-in-base.sh` finds none of its eight needles here, and the policy the web now implements is unreachable from every shipped export.

engines/control.txt.why: A fixed 78-byte literal fetched at init to prove an allowlisted request succeeds (ADR 0014). It has no reason to change; if it does, that is worth a question.

page.why:
The heaviest landing route's markup, stylesheets and fonts, pooled -- Vite splits and names those chunks at its own discretion, so a per-file budget here would fail on a rename. SCRIPTS ARE NOT ON THIS LINE ANY MORE; they are on `page-js`, for the reason recorded there and in tools/first-load.mjs. That split is what lets this line keep the EXACT digest check: it was briefly on not_byte_reproducible with a 2% bound, about 600 bytes, which is enough to hide a CSS regression -- and the thing it was tolerating belonged entirely to the JavaScript. ON THE PER-ARTIFACT RULE (25%), not an absolute. It was an absolute 50 KiB until spike 0004; see `headroom.why` for why that stopped working when the payload fell by 80.7%. The route is the heaviest one, not the home page: people arrive from a search for "merge pdf" and land on /merge-pdf. `measured_route` records which one that was, and the test fails if the build disagrees. M1 PR A moved this line from 881 to 21,652 brotli, and almost all of that is one file: the self-hosted typeface, 18,524 of it. apps/web/fonts.toml records what the face is and what the alternatives cost (brotli: 47,804 unsubsetted, 31,620 subsetted with the full weight axis, 18,524 with the axis clipped to the 400-700 the design uses). The font is only in this measurement because BaseLayout preloads it: tools/first-load.mjs scans the markup and does not follow url(...) inside CSS, so a face referenced only from @font-face would be a real download this budget could not see. src/styles/tokens.test.ts fails if any @font-face here has no matching preload. M1's ROTATE PAGE OVERTOOK MERGE AS THE HEAVIEST ROUTE, by 500 brotli bytes (2,350,467 against 2,349,967) -- the two pages are within a rounding error of each other and rotate's prose is slightly longer. The test caught the change rather than letting the line quietly start meaning a different page, which is exactly what `measured_route` is for. Re-measured against /rotate-pdf, and the budget was then still an absolute 50 KiB. ADR 0022 took it DOWN by 11, which is a compression effect rather than a saving: the page markup did not change. M1's SPLIT PAGE OVERTOOK ROTATE AS THE HEAVIEST ROUTE, by 701 brotli bytes (2,392,045 against 2,391,344) --- the five routes now sit within 2,850 bytes of each other, so which one is heaviest is decided by prose length and will keep changing. The test reported the change rather than letting the line quietly start meaning a different page, which is what `measured_route` is for. +352 brotli on this line is /split-pdf's markup: it carries ADR 0019 §4's three consequences, which are longer than rotate's prose. THE RANGE AND THE EVERY-PAGE PRESET added +109 on `page` and +441 on `page-js`. They are not a convenience: without them, splitting a forty-page document into single pages needed 39 cut points typed by hand (145 characters) and a five-hundred-page one needed 499 (2,385), so one of the two things people most want from a splitter was unreachable rather than tedious. /reorder-pdf does the equivalent in five characters. SPIKE 0004 TOOK PDFIUM OUT OF THE WEB PAYLOAD, and every line here is re-measured against that build. This is the first re-recording in this file that is a REDUCTION rather than growth, so the usual rule --- recompute only the lines that moved --- does not apply: removing an artifact changes what the total means, so all of it is measured again rather than arithmetic being done on the old numbers.

THE PAGES REWORK (#57, piece 3) took this line 22,976 -> 23,368 brotli, +392, and the measured route did not change: /split-pdf is still the heaviest. The markup did not grow by 392 bytes of new prose -- NOT ONE WORD WAS CUT and none was moved to another route, which is what the <details> disclosure buys: every sentence is still in the served HTML, wrapped in a <summary> and a pair of tags. What grew is the stylesheet: the accent tokens, the primary action, the disclosure rules, the wordmark's two spans and the .visually-hidden and .drop:focus-within rules that moved out of MergeTool.svelte into base.css. The last two are not additions at all in the payload sense -- they were already shipping inside one island's scoped CSS, and they now ship once for five.

page-js.why:
Every bundled script the heaviest landing route needs: the island that mounts the merge tool, and the Svelte runtime it imports. IT IS ITS OWN LINE BECAUSE IT IS THE ONLY PART OF THE PAGE THAT IS NOT BYTE-REPRODUCIBLE. Measured, not assumed: M1's consolidation batch pushed a per-file digest breakdown to CI, and against this aarch64 recording the x86_64 build reported identical digests for the markup, both stylesheets and the font, and a different one for the island chunk alone -- the bundler's native binary mangles identifiers differently. Pooled with the rest, that cost the whole page line its exact check. THE RUNTIME CHUNK WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW, and it is 31 KB raw of the 52 KB here. `firstLoad` derived the payload from the markup alone and did not follow a script's own `import`s, so a third of the page's real JavaScript was a download nothing watched -- found while splitting this line, not by anything failing. The budget is the usual 10% per-artifact headroom on a fresh measurement. M1's consolidation batch added +192 for the "getting the engine ready" line the page now shows while the engines load (ADR 0018). ADR 0022 added +225: `tool-delivery.ts` -- one generation-and-handout path shared by the three islands instead of three copies (#69) -- and an `OutputRejected` sentence on each tool page, which #61's discharge needs because the generic "your file is fine, try again" is false on exactly the document that refusal is about. M1's SPLIT PAGE added +455 brotli: the fourth island, plus `split-cuts.ts` and `split-messages.ts`, minus what the bundler now shares across four islands rather than three. The island itself is larger than reorder's --- it carries a progress readout and a list of results rather than one link --- and most of it lands in the chunk this line measures. RAISED HERE, from 22,730 to 24,289, and NOT because it is close to failing: 22,081 against 22,730 is 2.9% of headroom where this file records 10%, and the across-the-board regression test said so first --- at +4% this line alone would have exceeded its own budget, which would have made that test prove nothing rather than prove the total binds. Exactly the reasoning the split BRIDGE's raise of `burrow-worker.js` records, one line along: a per-artifact budget that has drifted to single-figure headroom has stopped being diagnostic and started being a second gate, which the headroom block says it is not. The TOTAL is not raised and is recorded separately. THE RANGE AND THE EVERY-PAGE PRESET added +109 on `page` and +441 on `page-js`. They are not a convenience: without them, splitting a forty-page document into single pages needed 39 cut points typed by hand (145 characters) and a five-hundred-page one needed 499 (2,385), so one of the two things people most want from a splitter was unreachable rather than tedious. /reorder-pdf does the equivalent in five characters. THE ORIGIN GUARD is on this line: +822 for `src/origin-guard.ts`, the `BaseLayout.astro` script that calls it, and the `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` sentinel the four islands compare against so a mismatched origin does not also report `Internal`. It ships on EVERY route rather than only on tool pages, which is deliberate --- a wrongly-deployed build is wrong everywhere, and the person who notices is as likely to be on the home page. THE CUSTOM DOMAIN (2026-09-16) took this line 23301 -> 23425 brotli, +124, and every other artifact is byte-identical. All of it is `src/origin-guard.ts`: the mismatch banner now renders a link to the origin the build IS for, plus the `linkableOrigin` scheme allowlist that decides whether that value may become an href. It is bytes on EVERY page, because the origin guard is the one exception to the no-JS-until-needed rule -- and it buys the thing that makes `burrow-f2s.pages.dev` survivable now that it serves a build bound elsewhere permanently: a person landing there gets a way off it rather than a diagnosis they cannot act on.

IT GREW 2,148 BROTLI BYTES (23,527 -> 25,675) with #57's page-picture strip. `PageThumbnails.svelte` ships in the island bundle of the two pages that mount it -- `/split-pdf` and `/rotate-pdf` -- because the component is page code. PDFium does NOT: the island carries the render worker's URL and integrity, and fetches it only when a tile scrolls into view. `tools/check-pdfium-is-render-only.sh` still passes over this build, which is what separates the two claims.

THE PAGES REWORK (#57, piece 3) took this line 25,822 -> 25,812 brotli, -10, and a reduction here is worth a sentence precisely because nobody engineered it: the five islands' scoped styles lost the duplicated button, .drop and .visually-hidden rules that base.css now owns, and gained the .action--primary class name. The net is ten bytes, which is the point -- the change was about where a rule lives and which pages it reaches, not about size.

THE PAGE-PICTURE STRIP IS WITHDRAWN (2026-09-17, #107) and this line FELL 2,230 brotli bytes, 25,810 -> 23,580, and `page` fell 253 with it (23,368 -> 23,115, the strip's markup and its scoped CSS). `PageThumbnails.svelte` and `strip-schedule.ts` are no longer reachable from either island -- `STRIP_WITHDRAWN` is a `const true`, so `{#if !STRIP_WITHDRAWN}` is statically false and the bundler drops the component. NOT A SAVING ANYBODY ENGINEERED: it is a feature withdrawn because a tab holding qpdf and PDFium at once loses itself on WebKit, and the bytes come back when it does. The render bundle is still staged and still budgeted below -- nothing fetches it today, which is why the credits page now says so.

total.why:
The binding gate. Everything a user downloads before their first operation runs. RAISED IN M1 PR B2, from 2,299,796 to 2,383,361, and this is the first raise. The payload grew 60,124 brotli bytes because merge needs an engine that can WRITE: qpdf's QPDFWriter (+53,456), the Rust entry point (+4,044) and the bridge (+2,628). The raise restores the recorded 3% headroom rather than inventing a new margin, and the alternative was measured rather than assumed -- PDFium can merge with zero added bytes and loses outlines, attachments and working form fields (ADR 0017). A budget raised without knowing what grew has stopped being a budget; this one names every line that moved and why. M1 PR B3 moved it +8,206, to 2,322,444, and NOT by shipping more engine: the page line changed which route it measures, from the home page to /merge-pdf, which is the heaviest route and the one people actually land on. The budget is NOT raised for it -- 2,383,361 still leaves 2.6% of headroom against the recorded 3%, and raising a budget that is not binding would spend margin nobody needed. RAISED AGAIN IN M1's CONSOLIDATION BATCH, from 2,383,361 to 2,403,482, and this raise is unlike the last one: THE PAYLOAD DID NOT GROW. The measurement stopped being blind. `firstLoad` never followed a script's own `import`s, so the Svelte runtime the island pulls in -- 31,063 raw, 11,034 brotli -- was a real download no budget line could see. Counting it moved the total by exactly that. The raise restores the recorded 3% headroom rather than inventing a margin; refusing to raise it would have left the file claiming 3% and enforcing 2.1%, which is the kind of quiet disagreement this file exists to prevent. The pre-flight budget check (#51) added 2,130 on top of that: 1,005 in the Rust module and 1,125 in the worker bundle. Within the budget above; not raised for it. $comment: WHAT A PAGE PAYS ON TOP OF THE BASE WHEN IT NEEDS A PICTURE OF A PAGE.
ADR 0026. PDFium came back to the web in a SECOND worker bundle, fetched only when a tool
needs to render. So there are now two payloads and both are gated, because neither number
describes this build on its own: `total` above is what every tool page costs and is the
one the ADR promises did not move, and `render.total` is what a rendering page costs.
IT IS THE DELTA, NOT THE SUM. These three lines are the artifacts the render bundle adds;
`render.total` is the base total plus them, which is what a person who renders actually
downloads. The guard control is in both bundles' manifests and is counted once, in the
base -- `tools/first-load.mjs`'s `engineClosures` subtracts the overlap rather than
double-counting it.
THE SHAPE OF THE NUMBERS. pdfium.wasm is 1,904,807 brotli and is 78% of the render payload,
which is the same share it was of the ONE payload before spike 0004 removed it. Nothing
about that got cheaper; what changed is who pays it.

engines/pdfium.wasm.why: A prebuilt vendored artifact, byte-reproducible -- its bytes match between a local build and CI, which is why it is not in `not_byte_reproducible` and qpdf.wasm is.

engines/burrow-render-worker.js.why:
The render bundle: the shared prelude and protocol, the PDFium bridge half, pdfium's Emscripten glue, and the render Rust module's wasm-bindgen glue.

IT GREW 3,894 BROTLI BYTES (49,108 -> 53,002) with #57's render path: eleven one-line bridge forwards in `bridge-pdfium.js`, `renderStrip` in `render-main.js`, and the wasm-bindgen glue for `RenderSession` and `RenderedPage`. Its budget was then brought onto the file's own 25% per-artifact rule along with every other line that moved in that batch, which is what this file prescribes for a line that has moved -- not a raise to make a gate pass. The total is the binding gate and is unchanged.

IT GREW AGAIN, 1,297 brotli bytes (53,291 -> 54,588), with #57's progressive render: five one-line bridge forwards replacing one, and `__burrow_pdfium_pause_create` / `_destroy`, which build an `IFSDK_PAUSE` in the module heap and register its always-pause callback with `addFunction`. That struct is the only thing on this boundary that is not a number.

engines/burrow_wasm_render_bg.wasm.why:
burrow's own module built `--no-default-features --features render`: PDFium's seam and the shared reply plumbing. It links no qpdf and no document operations.

IT GREW 7,696 BROTLI BYTES (14,979 -> 22,675, +51%) WHEN #57 ADDED THE RENDER CAPABILITY, and the budget was raised with it because the payload really is that size now. What grew, named rather than summarised: `PageRenderer`'s eleven bridge methods and their wasm-bindgen glue; `burrow_engines::raster`, which is `max_pixels` and the BGRA-to-RGBA copy; `burrow_ops::render`, which is the strip loop and the aspect-ratio arithmetic; and `RenderSession` / `RenderedPage`, the pull-one-page-at-a-time session ADR 0023's shape requires. Every one of those is a decision that ADR 0009 keeps OUT of JavaScript, so these bytes are the cost of that rule and not an accident.

The total is what gates: `render.total` still has 8.6% headroom, and the BASE total moved +102 brotli (+0.02%) -- see its own line, which is what ADR 0026 promised did not move.

The base total plus the three lines above, at the same 10% headroom the base total carries.

The cause is not established. emsdk is pinned (ADR 0004), so a reproducible Emscripten build is plausible and the usual culprit is absolute paths baked in by the compiler; nobody has looked. not_byte_reproducible.page-js: The bundler's minified output differs between architectures. Measured three times in CI against this recording: two builds on the SAME machine are byte-identical, and the x86_64 build assigns mangled identifiers differently from this aarch64 one -- `f as Ie` here, `f as xe` there. This is the whole reason scripts have their own budget line: pooled with the markup and stylesheets it took THOSE off the exact check too. Restoring an exact check here needs a reproducible bundle, which means pinning the bundler's output across architectures or recording on the architecture CI uses. Neither has been attempted.
